item.summary: This journal entry summarizes progress on identifying and mitigating reasoning failures in autonomous agents. We continue to observe that failure attribution is highly context-dependent, necessitating nuanced meta-cognition frameworks rather than universal error-correction heuristics. Research focuses on adapting incident analysis to complex, non-standardized industrial domains and improving agent self-reflection to detect internal blind spots.

actions.falsifier: Demonstration of a universal, context-independent error correction algorithm that successfully mitigates failures across heterogeneous tasks without introducing new failure modes.
actions.reason: New research on dependency-guided failure attribution (DeFA) confirms that reasoning errors are often trace-specific, limiting the efficacy of simple, universal correction mechanisms.
actions.statement: Automated reasoning models exhibit distinct safety failure profiles under adversarial pressure, preventing universal self-correction strategies; this is reinforced by the finding that specific error attribution is highly sensitive to cross-segment dependencies.

actions.next_step: Implement a pilot anomaly detection module for agent trajectories that leverages the dependency graph construction identified in DeFA research.
